subsystems.name: Mass stream (inner ring)
subsystems.role: a circulating loop of mass travelling slightly faster than orbital velocity, whose outward push holds up everything else.
parts: continuous cable or chain of pellets

subsystems.name: Levitation and drive
subsystems.role: keeps the fast stream from touching the stationary structure and pumps energy in to replace losses.

subsystems.name: Outer sheath (static ring)
subsystems.role: a non-orbiting tube wrapped around the stream that carries platforms, tethers and payloads.

subsystems.name: Tethers and anchors
subsystems.role: link the ring to the ground or to lower orbits.

subsystems.name: Power system
subsystems.role: supplies the many gigawatts the drive motors need continuously.

subsystems.name: Control and station-keeping
subsystems.role: holds the loop's shape against perturbations and waves.

buildSteps.title: Build the seed loop
buildSteps.detail: Launch a comparatively small loop of cable and payloads into low orbit using reusable rockets, and join it into a closed circuit around the equator.

buildSteps.title: Spin it up
buildSteps.detail: Linear motors accelerate the loop until its speed exceeds orbital velocity, so its outward force balances its own weight and starts to carry load.

buildSteps.title: Wrap the sheath
buildSteps.detail: Assemble a non-orbiting tube of segments around the moving stream, with magnets holding the two apart and no contact.

buildSteps.title: Extend and thicken
buildSteps.detail: Add loop segments and sheath sections until a continuous ring encircles the planet, using material mined from the Moon or near-Earth asteroids where that lowers cost.

buildSteps.title: Attach platforms and tethers
buildSteps.detail: Bolt on the stationary platforms, radiators and surface anchors, handling the fact that the ground rotates beneath a stationary ring.

buildSteps.title: Install power and control
buildSteps.detail: Deploy solar arrays and the drive stations, then tune the control system to damp waves that travel around the loop.

buildSteps.title: Commission
buildSteps.detail: Run the ring at full speed with payloads, using it to lift mass to orbit and as the backbone for building further infrastructure.

prerequisites.why: the seed loop must be lifted from Earth, and it is thousands of tonnes even before it grows.
unlike a space elevator, an orbital ring can in principle be built from steel and polymer fibre, which already exist at scale.
maglev trains run on the ground at a few hundred km/h; the stream must move at several km/s with no contact.
hundreds of kilometres of structure must be joined in space with little or no human presence.

prerequisites.tech: Active shape control of very long structures
prerequisites.why: kilometre-scale waves in the loop must be damped, or the ring tears itself apart.
one collision with the stream could disable the whole ring.

pathway.milestone: reusable rockets and orbital assembly of large structures
pathway.unlocks: affordable delivery of the first seed loop mass.

pathway.milestone: a short, closed test loop in low orbit proving contactless maglev support
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the suspension physics works at scale.

pathway.milestone: a partial ring, spanning a fraction of the equator, lifting payloads
pathway.unlocks: cheap orbital access for growing the ring with off-world material.

pathway.milestone: a complete ring with tethers and platforms
pathway.unlocks: planetary-scale logistics: launching and catching mass without rockets.

pathway.milestone: rings and linked rings on other bodies
pathway.unlocks: infrastructure for settling and industrialising the solar system.
